posts.title: Reference signal when measuring EEG
posts.b: When performing EEG, a number of electrodes are placed on the scalp to measure the electric potential difference between those locations and a reference. In the unipolar configuration, the reference is often the signal on another electrode (and is common to all measurement electrodes) or an average of the all measurement electrodes. In the bipolar configuration, the reference is specific to each measurement electrode (and is often another electrode located nearby). For examples, see here and here. posts.title: Does intermittent fasting increase intelligence?
posts.b: Intermittent fasting (IF) has been shown to offer several cognitive benefits, though it's important to clarify that it may not directly increase intelligence. Instead, IF can enhance brain function through processes like increased brain plasticity, neurogenesis (growth of new brain cells), and improved focus due to stabilized insulin levels. It also promotes the production of Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF), which supports learning and memory. For a deeper understanding of cognitive health and how lifestyle choices impact it, check out this video https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DPL2y4PIX04 on Alzheimer’s and learn more about early detection at Ivory.
